+# Flow 15 — Account settings, sign-out, and account deletion
+
+Date: 2026-10-22 (Asia/Qyzylorda)  
+Status: initial specification draft; owner decisions and operational policies remain OPEN  
+Mode: specification only; no product implementation, mockup, browser run, or verification is authorized or claimed
+
+## 1. Authority and scope
+
+This flow follows [the shared frontend contract](00-shared-contract.md), the latest owner answers recorded there, [SPEC-001](../specifications/SPEC-001_dubbed_mvp.md), and [BR-001](../business-requirements/BR-001_custom_video_dubbing.md) where later decisions have not replaced them.
+
+The screen lets an authenticated account owner:
+
+- switch the product interface between English and Russian;
+- inspect the Google and email/password methods associated with the account;
+- continue to the established verification, reset, or verified-linking flows when applicable;
+- sign out; and
+- start confirmed self-service account deletion.
+
+This flow does not add profile editing, a display name, avatar controls, notification preferences, appearance preferences, or unrelated settings.
+
+It does not restore Prepare, manual transcript/timing/speaker editing, missed-line addition, or background audition.
+
+## 2. Confirmed outcome and boundaries
+
+Account deletion is available at launch after confirmation.
+
+An authoritative successful deletion must:
+
+- disable owner access;
+- disable every public link belonging to the account;
+- remove the account's projects and recordings from user access; and
+- prevent late jobs, callbacks, or uploads from restoring deleted work or publishing a result.
+
+“Remove” here is a logical product outcome, not a promise that every physical copy disappears immediately.
+
+Backup, cache, CDN, security-record, and financial-record retention remain unspecified.
+
+Unused-credit, refund, reversal, purchase-history, and other balance treatment on account deletion also remain unspecified.
+
+Release-ready deletion copy and final destructive execution are blocked until those policies are approved and represented truthfully.
+
+## 3. Purpose, entry, and exit
+
+### 3.1 Purpose
+
+The screen's primary question is: **How can I control access to my account and close it safely?**
+
+The screen is a sparse settings view, not a profile dashboard, usage report, or marketing page.
+
+### 3.2 Entry
+
+The user selects Account in the authenticated compact top navigation.
+
+Entry requires an authenticated account context and an authoritative account-settings snapshot.
+
+If the session has expired, private account facts stay hidden and the user continues through Flow 02 before returning to the intended Account destination.
+
+### 3.3 Exits
+
+- Language change: remain on Account with the selected locale applied to the whole visible state.
+- Verify email: continue to Flow 03 with an explicit return destination.
+- Reset password: continue to Flow 04 if the owner selects that control for this screen.
+- Link a method: continue to Flow 05; never link from email equality alone.
+- Sign out: return to the signed-out entry defined by Flow 02.
+- Cancel deletion: close the confirmation and restore focus to Delete account.
+- Successful deletion: clear private client state and leave the authenticated application for a neutral signed-out/deleted-account destination.
+
+Exact route URLs and the post-deletion destination are OPEN.
+
+## 4. Screen anatomy and visual contract
+
+### 4.1 Shared shell
+
+Use the confirmed compact top navigation with product identity, New dub, My projects, credits balance/entry, and Account.
+
+Account is the active destination. There is no permanent sidebar.
+
+The account snapshot and the top-navigation balance must use the same authoritative account revision; the Account page does not invent a second balance.
+
+### 4.2 Content order
+
+1. `Account` noun title and one short scope sentence.
+2. Language.
+3. Sign-in methods.
+4. Session action: Sign out.
+5. Destructive action: Delete account, last and visually separate.
+
+The destructive section cannot appear before the account-access controls in visual, DOM, focus, or screen-reader order.
+
+### 4.3 Settings rows
+
+On wide screens, each area uses a label/description column beside one flat working panel.
+
+On narrow screens, the label stacks above its panel.
+
+Panels use either a quiet tone step or a quiet border, not a resting shadow plus border.
+
+Use flat white/light-gray surfaces, readable black/near-black text, and no gradients, glass, glow, decorative illustration, vanity metrics, charts, or icon-topped cards.
+
+Red is reserved for destructive meaning and deletion failure; it is not a section background texture.
+
+Exact fonts, sizes, hex values, widths, radii, gaps, breakpoints, and control geometry remain OPEN in the shared design system.
+
+### 4.4 Product-specific substance
+
+The screen shows the real current locale, verified account identifier where required by the login-method row, and the real association state of Google and email/password.
+
+It does not show sample identities, fabricated account age, security scores, or invented usage figures.
+
+## 5. Language control
+
+The Language area contains one mutually exclusive English / Russian control with an accessible group name.
+
+Selecting a language updates navigation, headings, actions, dialog content, status, loading text, and errors as one locale; mixed-language states are invalid.
+
+The control must not change audio-language detection or project media.
+
+While a persisted locale change is pending, the UI must expose a truthful saving state if persistence is part of the eventual service contract.
+
+On failure, preserve or restore the last authoritative locale and offer Retry without discarding other Account state.
+
+Cross-device locale persistence, reload fallback, and signed-out locale ownership are OPEN shared-shell decisions.
+

+
+### 6.1 Method rows
+
+Show exactly two supported method families:

+| Method | Facts shown | Available continuation |
+|---|---|---|
+| Google | Associated / not associated / verification or linking in progress / unavailable | Continue to Flow 05 when linking is allowed; reauthentication belongs to Flow 02 or Flow 05 |
+| Email and password | Verified email / verification pending / not associated / unavailable | Flow 03 for verification; Flow 04 for self-service reset if selected for this page; Flow 05 for linking |
+

+
+The identity service supplies the authoritative association and verification state.
+
+An interrupted linking attempt remains a Flow 05 concern; Account may show its returned status but does not duplicate that flow.
+
+### 6.2 Unknown method-management policy
+
+Whether Account exposes a Reset password action, an inline password-change form, or no password action for Google-only accounts is OPEN-F15-Q2.
+
+Whether either login method can be unlinked here, and the last-method protection, are OPEN-F15-Q3.
+
+Until resolved, no Unlink control is required and no acceptance criterion may claim unlinking works.
+
+The confirmed verified-linking entry may remain available through Flow 05 without implying unlink support.
+
+## 7. Sign out
+
+Sign out is a distinct session action, not part of the destructive section.
+
+Selecting Sign out sends one session-termination request and shows a pending state on that action.
+
+On authoritative success, clear private account/project/balance state from the active client and navigate to the signed-out entry.
+
+On failure or timeout, do not claim sign-out success; keep the user on Account, explain that sign-out could not be confirmed, and offer Retry.
+
+If the server reports the session already absent, reconcile to the signed-out state.
+
+Reload during an uncertain sign-out checks the authoritative session rather than trusting a stale client flag.
+
+## 8. Account deletion confirmation
+
+### 8.1 Known consequence disclosure
+
+Before the final destructive action, the confirmation must state that deletion:
+
+- ends account access;
+- removes every account project and recording from product access;
+- disables all existing shared links; and
+- cannot be undone through the product.
+
+The dialog must not promise immediate erasure from backups, caches, logs, financial records, or external systems.
+
+The approved balance, financial-record, security-record, backup, and cache policy must be added before release.
+
+### 8.2 Confirmation sequence
+
+1. User selects Delete account.
+2. An accessible dialog on desktop or bottom sheet on phone names the account and complete known consequences.
+3. User completes the owner-selected confirmation/reauthentication factor.
+4. The final action remains explicitly named Delete account / Удалить аккаунт.
+5. The client submits one idempotent deletion operation bound to the authenticated account and current revision.
+6. The client reconciles the authoritative outcome before retrying after an ambiguous timeout.
+
+The confirmation factor is OPEN-F15-Q1; password, provider reauthentication, typed confirmation, or a combination cannot be selected by this draft.
+
+Closing, Escape, or Cancel before submission performs no deletion and returns focus to the initiating button.
+
+Once authoritative account disablement succeeds, the frontend must not restore private content even if physical cleanup is still pending.
+
+### 8.3 Deletion states
+
+| State | Visible behavior | Protection |
+|---|---|---|
+| Closed | Destructive section with consequence summary and Delete account | No destructive request |
+| Reviewing | Full consequence text, Cancel, and the selected verification control | Final action follows the disclosure in reading/focus order |
+| Verification failed | Specific recoverable message; consequences remain visible | No deletion request |
+| Submitting | Final action disabled with plain progress text | Prevent duplicate clicks; keep operation identity |
+| Outcome unknown | Say deletion could not yet be confirmed; Retry checks status first | No blind duplicate destructive request |
+| Rejected/stale | Explain that account state changed; reload authoritative snapshot | No client-side override |
+| Disabled/deleted | Remove private UI and leave authenticated shell | No account resurrection from cached state |
+
+## 9. Loading, stale, failure, and reload behavior
+
+### 9.1 Initial loading
+
+Render the final section structure with headings immediately and flat placeholders at their final sizes.
+
+Do not show guessed method associations, email, balance, or deletion eligibility while loading.
+
+### 9.2 Partial failure
+
+Keep each failed area in place with one concrete message and Retry.
+
+Failure to load login methods must not hide the Language or Sign out controls if their own authoritative state is available.
+
+Failure to load deletion policy or eligibility disables Delete account and states why.
+
+### 9.3 Stale and concurrent state
+
+Method, locale, session, and deletion commands carry the expected account revision or equivalent stale-write protection.
+
+If another tab/device changes a method or deletes the account, refresh to the authoritative state; never overwrite it with the old screen.
+
+If a different account signs in during a return from verification or linking, stop the continuation and do not disclose the previous account's facts.
+
+### 9.4 Reload and recovery
+
+Reload reconstructs from server-owned session and account state.
+
+It does not replay a password reset, linking, sign-out, or deletion command from component memory.
+
+A reload during pending/unknown deletion reconciles by operation identity and account status before offering any retry.
+
+## 10. Visible copy and localization
+
+The baseline labels are:
+
+| English | Russian |
+|---|---|
+| Account | Аккаунт |
+| Language | Язык |
+| English | English |
+| Russian | Русский |
+| Sign-in methods | Способы входа |
+| Email and password | Электронная почта и пароль |
+| Verify email | Подтвердить почту |
+| Reset password | Сбросить пароль |
+| Link | Подключить |
+| Sign out | Выйти |
+| Delete account | Удалить аккаунт |
+| Cancel | Отмена |
+| Try again | Повторить |

+
+Final method-status wording, account-identification wording, deletion consequence copy, retention disclosure, and post-deletion copy require localization review after the OPEN policies resolve.
+
+Errors use plain active language, name what failed, and say what the user can do next.
+

+
+- Desktop uses the shared compact top navigation and a bounded settings canvas; no sidebar appears.
+- Tablet folds the shared navigation according to the shared-shell contract before panels become too narrow.

+- No page-level horizontal scrolling is allowed at 390 px, 200% zoom, or with long Russian copy.
+- The deletion sheet and its actions remain visible above the on-screen keyboard and safe areas.
+- DOM, reading, and focus order follow the content order in §4.2.
+- Every control has a visible focus state, programmatic name, current state, disabled reason, and status announcement where state changes asynchronously.
+- Radio/segmented language choices expose one selected value; login-method status is text, not color alone.
+- The deletion dialog traps focus, has an accessible name and description, supports Cancel/Escape before submission, and returns focus correctly.
+- Motion is limited to direct feedback such as dialog/sheet opening; reduced-motion users receive no unnecessary travel.
+
+## 12. Logical frontend services
+
+The frontend depends on replaceable service interfaces rather than importing transport details into components.
+
+| Service | Inputs | Required results |
+|---|---|---|
+| `AccountSettingsService.load` | current authenticated context | account revision, locale, method associations/verification, deletion eligibility and approved disclosure revision |
+| `LocaleService.set` | account, locale, expected revision, operation ID | authoritative locale/revision or stale/failure result |
+| `SessionService.signOut` | session and operation ID | terminated/already absent/failure/unknown |
+| `IdentityService` | current account and continuation target | Flow 03/04/05 continuation and reconciled method state |
+| `AccountDeletionService.start` | account, expected revision, disclosure revision, confirmation evidence, operation ID | rejected/pending/disabled/completed/unknown |
+| `AccountDeletionService.status` | account/deletion operation ID where still authorized | reconciled outcome without repeating deletion |
+
+Deletion orchestration must fence project workers, uploads, results, sharing, and late events through backend/application services.
+
+A future mock must label itself as a mock, use deterministic fixtures, and exercise pending, stale, timeout, and failure states.

+A mock is not proof of live Google, email delivery, password reset, cross-device state, public-link disablement, data cleanup, or account deletion.
+
+No backend, security, retention, billing, or external-provider implementation is created by this specification.
+

+
+- Current projects, accepted takes, and account-owned unaccepted recording drafts have no inactivity expiry.
+- They remain until acceptance where applicable, explicit draft/project deletion, or account deletion.
+- A validated but unprocessed upload remains a My projects draft and occupies its slot until project/account deletion.
+- Account deletion removes those projects and recordings from access and disables their shared links.
+- Private account identifiers, method state, balance, projects, and deletion evidence must not appear in public viewer state, public errors, analytics payloads, or URLs.
+- Credentials, reset tokens, provider tokens, confirmation evidence, signed-media URLs, and raw security records never render in the settings UI or logs.
+- Exact physical cleanup and legally/operationally retained-record policies remain OPEN.
+

+- [ ] **F15-AC09 — Responsive and accessible:** the complete EN/RU screen and confirmation work by keyboard and assistive technology at desktop, tablet, 390 px phone, 200% zoom, and reduced viewport height.
+- [ ] **F15-AC10 — Privacy:** private account, identity, balance, token, and deletion evidence stays out of public state, URLs, and user-visible logs/errors.
+- [ ] **F15-AC11 — Honest mock boundary:** deterministic mocks visibly remain mocks and do not claim live provider, email, deletion, retention, or public-link evidence.
+- [ ] **F15-AC12 — Visual contract:** rendered states follow the approved shared tokens and geometry, flat light settings hierarchy, reserved destructive red, and no gradients/sidebar. **BLOCKED until shared visual decisions and rendered evidence exist.**
+

+

+| Shared shell / Flow 01 | Product identity, top navigation, locale entry, responsive shell, eventual tokens |
+| Flow 02 — Sign in | Authenticated account/session, reauthentication, expired-session return |

+## 9. Loading, stale, failure, and reload
+
+Initial loading keeps final section structure/headings and flat placeholders at final size. Do not guess email, method associations, balance, or deletion eligibility.
+
+Keep each failed area in place with one concrete message and Retry. One area failing does not hide independently authorized controls. Failure to load deletion policy or eligibility disables Delete account and says why.
+
+Locale, method, session, and deletion mutations carry expected revision or equivalent stale-write protection. Another tab/device change reloads authoritative state; the old screen never overwrites it.
+
+If a different account signs in during verification/linking return, stop and reveal none of the prior account's facts.
+
+Reload reconstructs from server-owned session/account state and never replays reset, linking, sign-out, or deletion from component memory. Pending/unknown deletion reconciles by operation identity before retry.
+

+| Account | Аккаунт |
+| Language | Язык |

+| Russian | Русский |

+| Link | Подключить |
+| Sign out | Выйти |
+| Delete account | Удалить аккаунт |
+| Cancel | Отмена |
+| Try again | Повторить |
+

+
+Errors use plain active language, name what failed, and state the next action.
+
+## 11. Desktop, phone, keyboard, and assistive technology
+
+- Desktop uses top navigation and a bounded settings canvas; no sidebar.
+- Tablet folds navigation before panels become too narrow.
+- Phone uses 16–20 px margins, stacks labels above panels, and keeps targets at least 44 px tall.
+- No page-level horizontal scroll at 390 px, 200% zoom, or with long Russian copy.
+- Deletion content/actions remain visible above keyboard and safe areas.
+- Every control has visible focus, programmatic name/state, disabled reason, and async status announcement.
+- Language exposes one selected value; method/deletion status never relies on color alone.
+- Confirmation traps focus, has name/description, supports Cancel/Escape before submission, and restores focus.
+- Motion is direct feedback only; reduced motion removes unnecessary travel.
+
+## 12. Logical frontend services
+
+Components depend on replaceable logical services, not transport details:
+
+| Service | Inputs | Results |
+|---|---|---|
+| `AccountSettingsService.load` | authenticated context | revision, locale, method states, deletion eligibility/disclosure revision |
+| `LocaleService.set` | account, locale, revision, operation ID | authoritative locale/revision or stale/failure |

+| `AccountDeletionService.status` | deletion operation identity | reconciled outcome without repeating deletion |
+
+Backend/application services must fence projects, workers, uploads, results, sharing, and late events.

+A future mock must label itself, use deterministic fixtures, and cover pending, stale, timeout, and failure. It is not proof of live Google, email, reset, cross-device state, link disablement, cleanup, or deletion. This spec creates no backend or security implementation.
+
+## 13. Persistence and privacy
+
+- Current projects, accepted takes, and account-owned unaccepted recording drafts have no inactivity expiry.
+- They remain until applicable acceptance, explicit draft/project deletion, or account deletion.
+- A validated unprocessed upload remains in My projects and occupies its slot until project/account deletion.
+- Account deletion removes those projects/recordings from access and disables their links.
+- Private identifiers, methods, balance, projects, and deletion evidence stay out of public viewer state, public errors, analytics, and URLs.
+- Credentials, reset/provider tokens, confirmation evidence, signed-media URLs, and raw security records never render or enter user-visible logs.
+- Exact physical cleanup and retained-record policies remain OPEN.
